## Before you start

- **Designed for:** learners with little or no programming experience.
- **You are ready when:** you can use a browser and are willing to predict, run,
  explain, modify, quiz, and debug small examples. No mathematics prerequisite
  is assumed.
- **Practice setup:** begin with generated Colab notebooks. Unit 0 compares
  notebook and local workflows before later units introduce full projects.
- **Assessment:** lesson checkpoints diagnose understanding; each unit challenge
  asks you to integrate its ideas with assertions, hints, and debugging evidence.

## What you will be able to do

- read Python syntax and trace values, state, decisions, loops, calls, and object relationships;
- choose representations for numbers, text, time, collections, files, and external records;
- turn requirements into small algorithms, functions, modules, packages, and classes;
- diagnose failures from tracebacks and controlled experiments;
- build a reproducible Git-backed project with a CLI and layered tests;
- improve behavior safely with typing, formatting, linting, quality gates, and refactoring; and
- create verified README, API, executable, and published documentation.

## Learning sequence

Python Foundations curriculum version 11 contains **16 units** and
**89 cohesive lessons**. Each unit begins with an Overview and
ends with a challenge.

| Unit | Focus | Outcome | Apply it |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 0 | [Get Started](units/get-started/index.qmd) | Choose a dependable learning environment and use prediction, execution, explanation, modification, debugging, and responsible AI assistance as a repeatable learning loop. | [Challenge](units/get-started/challenge.qmd) |
| 1 | [Learning to Read and Write Python Code](units/python-syntax/index.qmd) | Read a short program, trace how Python interprets it, format its structure clearly, document its decisions, and repair syntax errors systematically. | [Challenge](units/python-syntax/challenge.qmd) |
| 2 | [Numbers, Text, and Other Values](units/core-values-types/index.qmd) | Choose suitable Python values for counts, measurements, money, text, truth, missing information, and time; convert and format them deliberately; and explain important precision, parsing, and comparison boundaries. | [Challenge](units/core-values-types/challenge.qmd) |
| 3 | [Organizing and Traversing Collections](units/collections-iteration/index.qmd) | Choose among lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets from order, mutability, lookup, uniqueness, and data shape; traverse them safely; and sort or combine them without losing relationships. | [Challenge](units/collections-iteration/challenge.qmd) |
| 4 | [Making Decisions and Repeating Work](units/decisions-repetition/index.qmd) | Turn written rules into complete, non-overlapping branches; use loops to transform, search, and traverse data; and explain how each loop progresses and stops. | [Challenge](units/decisions-repetition/challenge.qmd) |
| 5 | [Building Reusable Functions](units/functions-call-behavior/index.qmd) | Design, call, compose, and trace reusable functions with clear parameters, returned results, documented contracts, and controlled side effects; pass behavior as data; and explain how recursive, lazy, closure-based, and decorated calls progress and finish. | [Challenge](units/functions-call-behavior/challenge.qmd) |
| 6 | [Sharing, Changing, and Copying Objects](units/mutability-identity-copying/index.qmd) | Trace which names and containers share objects; distinguish equality, identity, rebinding, mutation, immutability, and hashability; choose shallow, selective, or deep copying from an explicit ownership contract; and design functions whose mutations or returned copies are deliberate and observable. | [Challenge](units/mutability-identity-copying/challenge.qmd) |
| 7 | [Problem Solving and Basic Algorithms](units/problem-solving-algorithms/index.qmd) | Convert an ambiguous task into examples, constraints, an algorithm, small functions, and evidence that the result handles important boundaries. | [Challenge](units/problem-solving-algorithms/challenge.qmd) |
| 8 | [Errors, Exceptions, and Debugging](units/errors-exceptions-debugging/index.qmd) | Distinguish failure categories, read tracebacks, handle only anticipated failures, and debug one evidence-backed hypothesis at a time. | [Challenge](units/errors-exceptions-debugging/challenge.qmd) |
| 9 | [Files, Paths, and External Data](units/files-paths-external-data/index.qmd) | Cross text, binary, file, and structured-data boundaries explicitly, using paths, encodings, validation, and managed resources safely. | [Challenge](units/files-paths-external-data/challenge.qmd) |
| 10 | [Modules, Environments, and Python Projects](units/modules-environments-projects/index.qmd) | Find reusable functionality, split code across modules, organize a versioned project, isolate dependencies, and explain how source becomes an installable distribution. | [Challenge](units/modules-environments-projects/challenge.qmd) |
| 11 | [Object-Oriented Python and Dataclasses](units/object-oriented-python/index.qmd) | Decide when a class improves a model, design objects with valid state and clear behavior, and prefer composition when inheritance adds unnecessary coupling. | [Challenge](units/object-oriented-python/challenge.qmd) |
| 12 | [Command-Line Applications](units/command-line-applications/index.qmd) | Build a composable command with explicit arguments, streams, exit status, logging, configuration, and a testable core. | [Challenge](units/command-line-applications/challenge.qmd) |
| 13 | [Testing Python Programs](units/testing-python-programs/index.qmd) | Design fast, meaningful tests at appropriate boundaries and use failures to improve behavior without coupling tests to implementation trivia. | [Challenge](units/testing-python-programs/challenge.qmd) |
| 14 | [Code Quality and Maintainability](units/code-quality-maintainability/index.qmd) | Make behavior-preserving improvements using readable conventions, types, automated checks, and evidence rather than taste alone. | [Challenge](units/code-quality-maintainability/challenge.qmd) |
| 15 | [Documentation as Part of the Product](units/documentation-publishing/index.qmd) | Create and publish documentation that helps distinct audiences learn, complete tasks, understand design, and use a stable API. | [Challenge](units/documentation-publishing/challenge.qmd) |

## Assessment and progress

Treat each lesson as a lab: predict, run, explain, modify, quiz, and debug. A
unit challenge then asks you to select and combine ideas rather than repeat a
lesson example. Unit 0 concludes with a methodology and setup quiz. The other
challenges are designed for 60–120 minutes and provide a public contract,
progressive checks, three hint levels, and a debugging-evidence record.

The progress dashboard is private, self-reported browser storage. It does not
submit work, grade artifacts, verify identity, or issue credentials.

::: {.callout-important title="Final project and certificate are coming later"}
A Python Foundations final project and certificate are planned. Requirements,
availability, and participation details will be announced soon.
:::

## Start learning

Begin with the learning method, then move through the units in order. Return to
earlier evidence whenever a later task exposes a gap.
